title: Multiteam leads sync — reflections and actions
body:
Meeting: Multiteam leads sync (informal) — notes and next steps
Date: 2026-06-18 09:30-10:15 PT
Location: Zoom / #leads-sync
Facilitator: Aisha
Attendees: Aisha, Jamal, Mei, Omar, Lina (SRE), Priya (Serving Runtime), Ben (Private), Carlos (Solutions eng)

High-level goal: quick alignment across platform, serving runtime, private deployments, and SRE on near-term risks, capacity, and any cross-team escalations. Keep it ~45m, focus on decisions and owners.

Topline updates (2-minute roundtrips)
- Platform-engineering (Aisha): Canary rollout of autoscaler v2 started; observed 10% under-provisioning at 3am window (small burst). Investigating policy edge-cases.
- Serving-runtime (Priya): New kernel shim landed in staging; perf +/- 4% on 8k tokens in our microbench. Need a small safety window before wide rollout.
- Private (Ben): First on-prem pilot customer onboarding delayed due to KMS handshake issues in their network; working with customer infra and our network team.
- SRE (Lina): Two Sev2s last week — both due to transient KV cache corruption after a redeploy. Patch in testing.

Discussion notes (bulleted, rough)
- Autoscaler under-provisioning root cause hypothesis: policy math + burst window config. Jamal suggested a short-term mitigator: temporary increase to min_provision on critical zones for next 48h. Agreed.
- Kernel shim: rollout plan options — aggressive (fast rollout with quick rollback hooks) vs conservative (canary across 3 clusters over 2 weeks). Decision: conservative. Priya to draft canary checklist.
- Private onboarding: blocked by KMS handshake timing-out when customer HSM returns slow. Ben exploring an exponential backoff + extended timeouts option; security team raised concerns about making timeouts too long. Action: Ben + Security to propose a hardened handshake retry policy tomorrow.
- KV cache corruption: likely race during parallel warm-up after deploy. Lina proposes feature-flagged sequential warm-up in hot paths. Concern: slows deploys. Tradeoff approved for immediate patch.

Risk radar (things we should watch this week)
- Capacity: potential bump in load from partner beta (marketing email scheduled Fri). If conversion to hosted spikes, we could exceed dedicated pool limits in us-west-2. Quick ask: Solutions Eng to gate partner traffic and throttle if utilization > 85%. Owner: Carlos.
- Quality regressions: new kernel shim might change sampling distribution for long contexts. Add focused evals to smoke tests (prompt sets: long-chat-regen). Owner: Mei.
- Enterprise sales demo (Wed): need Private environment ready with KMS flow; if unresolved, sales will request alternate demo. Owner: Ben + Sales engineer liaison.

Decisions made
- Autoscaler: increase min_provision in critical zones for 48h (Jamal).
- Kernel shim: conservative canary rollout (Priya + Serving runtime).
- Temporary sequential warm-up to prevent KV corruption; will measure and iterate (Lina).

Action items (owner — due)
- Jamal: apply min_provision bump to us-west-2 for critical pools and monitor 2x daily metrics (due: 2026-06-18 EOD).
- Priya: produce canary checklist + rollback plan for kernel shim and post to PR 901 (due: 2026-06-19).
- Ben: coordinate with Security on KMS handshake retry policy and produce proposal (due: 2026-06-19).
- Lina: open a follow-up ticket to implement sequential warm-up behind feature flag and run perf diff (ticket: PLTF-4899) (due: 2026-06-20).
- Carlos: prepare a throttling rule for partner beta traffic and coordinate with Growth to delay email if thresholds hit (due: 2026-06-19).
- Mei: add long-context evals to smoke suite and run baseline against current main and shim branch (due: 2026-06-20).

Parking lot / follow-ups
- Revisit autoscaler policy math in next week’s architecture forum (owner: Aisha).
- Discuss longer-term rollout automation for kernel changes (owner: Priya).
- Draft an incident postmortem template for KV cache corruption once patch validated (owner: Lina).

Notes to self / informal thoughts
- Keep the meeting short and decision-focused; we spent ~10 minutes on minor rollout scheduling — tighten agenda.
- Consider a one-page "risk snapshot" emailed on Fridays showing utilization curves and top 3 risks — could reduce meeting duration.

Metrics snapshot (quick numbers pulled during meeting)
- 99th p95 token latency (hosted): 188ms (up 6% week-over-week during peak).
- Dedicated pool us-west-2 avg utilization: 62% (spiky at 91% last Saturday at 03:00 PT).
- Recent deploy success rate (last 7 days): 94% (target > 98%).
- KV-cache related incidents: 2 (both Sev2)

Attachments referenced / quick links
- PLTF-4821 (autoscaler rollout ticket)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/901 (kernel shim)
- Confluence: June Release Plan (link in header)

Next meeting: 2026-06-25 09:30 PT
Requested pre-reads: brief bullet updates in the shared doc by EOD Tue (autoscaler, kernel shim canary plan, KMS retry policy).

End notes: short-term stabilization prioritized this week — minimize risky broad rollouts. Keep escalation channel open in #incidents for any regression observed after autoscaler bump.

----
Versioning: working notes — will convert to finalized staff brief if items close cleanly by 06-21.
